recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the published clarification in an active build source file without changing conformance structure, and it aligns narrative guidance with the existing definition, search parameter, and later optional qualification.status element.
issue_request: FHIR-36681 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested clarification on whether to send a license identifier when active status is unknown, when to use Practitioner.identifier versus Practitioner.qualification.identifier, why qualification.identifier is repeatable, and removal of the misleading "in this role" definition wording.
initial_application: Commit 6e58083f0879ea3b5ad74e25e7a10eb64f0b0ab2 removed "in this role" from Practitioner.qualification.identifier. Related earlier/later source already had FHIR-32493 identifier-placement notes and FHIR-32494 search-parameter coverage, but the notes still lacked the multiple-identifier rationale and ambiguous unknown-status guidance remained.
additional_context: Practitioner is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-34375 later added optional Practitioner.qualification.status, so the FHIR-36681 note can now explicitly say to omit status when unknown and use Practitioner.qualification child elements when details are known. PA May 2022 WGM minutes support the persuasive disposition and identify FHIR-36680 as duplicate/search context; no conflicting Zulip or Confluence discussion was found.
reconciliation: Changed source/practitioner/practitioner-notes.xml to clarify that business identifiers may be in either or both identifier locations; Practitioner.identifier does not by itself convey qualification details beyond identifier metadata; known qualification details belong in Practitioner.qualification child elements; unknown status is omitted; multiple qualification identifiers can represent certifying-body and internal-system identifiers; profiles may constrain cardinality; and the identifier search parameter includes both paths.
source_changes: source/practitioner/practitioner-notes.xml: clarified Practitioner identifier versus qualification identifier usage, unknown qualification status handling, repeatable qualification.identifier rationale, profile cardinality constraints, and identifier search behavior.
